transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 14:30 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Tom Hargreaves (Rivergate Head of Infra), Priya Kapoor (Platform Eng), Ethan Morris (CISO)

Summary (auto):
Initial discovery focused on Dedicated capacity for Rivergate's LLM inference workloads. Key topics: reserved GPUs, isolation and network requirements (VPC), burst/burst-to-hosted strategy, scaling expectations, SOC2/compliance, and benchmark next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we really appreciate the time. Quick intros?
[00:06] Tom Hargreaves: Tom, Head of Infrastructure at Rivergate, we run the ML infra and platform.
[00:09] Priya Kapoor: Priya, platform eng, I own the runtime and CI/CD around model serving.
[00:12] Ethan Morris: Ethan, CISO, security and compliance.
[00:14] Diego Alvarez: Diego, Redwood solutions engineering. I'll try to stay out of Maya's way but I'll jump in for the technical bits.
[00:19] Maya Chen: Cool, thanks. The goal for today is to understand your workload and see whether Dedicated or Private makes sense, and what the reserved capacity and burst policies would look like.
[00:27] Tom Hargreaves: Yeah, we have a few production routes already using hosted APIs but at scale cost and data isolation are concerns. We're evaluating reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput.
[00:37] Priya Kapoor: For context our primary workloads are conversational support (latency sensitive), and nightly batch reranking for search. The conv path is small requests, high QPS, bursts during peak hours, latency target sub-200ms p50, p95 < 500ms. The rerank jobs are high token counts but offline, we can tolerate longer tails.
[00:55] Diego Alvarez: Got it. Do you have any numbers on peak concurrency or tokens-per-minute?
[00:59] Priya Kapoor: Roughly 1200 concurrent small chats at peak across our web and mobile channels, maybe 8k requests per minute, avg request 40 tokens, embeddings for search run once an hour for new docs. Monthly token estimate around 1.2B tokens.
[01:13] Maya Chen: That's helpful. On Dedicated we usually size for concurrent streams and KV cache behavior; for chat we look at the sequence lengths and model choice because that drives memory and throughput. Which models are you evaluating?
[01:24] Tom Hargreaves: Internally we tried an open Llama variant and some tuned 7b-ish stacks; for higher quality trials we used a couple commercial endpoints. We want Redwood to support both open weights and your curated models.
[01:34] Diego Alvarez: We can support both, and on Dedicated you can pin specific model versions. For your throughput numbers a 4x A100-equivalent pool or 2x H100 depending on quantization and batching could meet p95 latencies but we should run benchmarks.
[01:48] Ethan Morris: Quick security note: any dedicated environment must be VPC-isolated, have customer-managed KMS, audit logs that are immutable, RBAC integration with our SSO (SAML). We also need SOC 2 type II evidence.
[01:59] Maya Chen: Understood. Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering or Private deployment for tighter networking. We do KMS integration for key wrapping, and we can provide audit logs and SAML SSO. We have SOC 2 reports and can share the pack.
[02:09] Priya Kapoor: Two network questions: 1) can we force egress through our transit gateway? 2) can you guarantee zero shared tenancy for GPUs? We want cryptographic isolation and no co-tenancy for inference.
[02:19] Diego Alvarez: Dedicated means reserved hardware for your account; there won't be multi-tenant inference co-located on those GPUs. For egress you can set up VPC peering and route tables to force traffic; Private on-prem would be absolute isolation but Dedicated within the cloud still gives you dedicated capacity plus network controls.
[02:35] Tom Hargreaves: How does burst work? Our traffic is spiky and we don't want queued requests when we exceed reserved capacity. We might want burst to hosted Redwood for overflow but with fallbacks on model quality.
[02:46] Maya Chen: We offer burst-to-hosted as a policy: when dedicated pool is saturated requests route to the hosted tier to preserve latency. You can configure routing by model variant, by region, and set hard caps. The tradeoff is that hosted may have different model variants and different data residency controls; we can surface that in the routing policy.
[03:04] Priya Kapoor: Is there a cold-start / scaling penalty when we autoscale Dedicated? We prefer a predictable pool rather than autoscale that spins new instances.
[03:11] Diego Alvarez: Dedicated pools are typically reserved instances kept warm; autoscaling adds capacity but with a few minutes of lead time. For low-latency chat you usually keep the pool warm and use burst-to-hosted for spikes so you don't hit cold starts.
[03:23] Ethan Morris: On compliance, we can't ship PII to hosted endpoints unless it's encrypted at rest with our keys. Does Redwood support envelope encryption with customer KMS for hosted fallback?
[03:33] Maya Chen: For Hosted fallback we can implement client-side encryption or envelope encryption integration; for Dedicated we support customer KMS for at-rest and in-transit protections. We'll include the KMS whitepaper in the follow-up.
[03:43] Tom Hargreaves: Pricing: give me ballpark OPEX for a 4x A100-equivalent dedicated pool vs burst-to-hosted costs. Also commitment terms — monthly or annual?
[03:52] Maya Chen: I'll send formal pricing, but typically monthly reserved pools can be monthly or annual with discounts for annual. The cost depends on GPU class and utilization. For cost modeling we'll produce an estimate with your token numbers and expected utilization.
[04:04] Priya Kapoor: About model updates and rollouts: we need canary and rollback and ability to pin model versions per route. Is that available?
[04:10] Diego Alvarez: Yes, rollouts, canaries, A/B tests per route are part of our console; you can pin model versions and set automatic fallback policies. We also expose tracing so you can see per-token latencies.
[04:21] Priya Kapoor: What about KV cache persistence between restarts? We need sessions to be fast for multi-turn chat without re-computing context.
[04:27] Diego Alvarez: Our runtime supports KV cache warmup and shared cache for sessions on Dedicated. For cross-instance sessions you'd configure sticky routing or session pinning.
[04:35] Tom Hargreaves: Any limits on concurrent streaming connections? We want websocket-style streaming to web clients.
[04:41] Maya Chen: We support streaming responses and can handle high concurrency; sizing depends on pods and concurrent streams per GPU. We'll capture that in the benchmark config.
[04:50] Ethan Morris: Can you confirm log retention windows and redaction? We need logs retained for 90 days and the ability to redact PII before logs leave our VPC.
[04:59] Maya Chen: We can configure log retention and provide pre-ingest redaction hooks. For Private on-prem installs you keep logs entirely in your environment.
[05:07] Priya Kapoor: Two more technical points: do you support quantized models (INT8/4) to increase throughput? And what's the impact on quality?
[05:14] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we support quantized execution paths. There's usually a small quality delta; our Optimize team provides quantization profiles and recommendations by workload. We'll propose specific quant settings in the benchmark.
[05:25] Tom Hargreaves: Our timeline: we'd like to pilot in April, then production by June. Decision depends on benchmark results and legal review.
[05:34] Maya Chen: That timeline sounds reasonable. Proposed next step is a 1-week benchmark on Dedicated with your sample traffic, then review results, plus we send SOC 2 and pricing.
[05:43] Priya Kapoor: For the benchmark we'll need the load script and an expected success criteria doc: p50/p95 latency, error rate under 0.5%, and throughput hitting at least 80% of peak.
[05:54] Diego Alvarez: Noted. We'll include load scripts and an agreement on success metrics.
[05:59] Tom Hargreaves: One last question: data residency. Some of our EU customers require data to remain in EU. Can Dedicated be region pinned?
[06:06] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated pools can be region pinned and we support region-based routing. For stricter requirements we can discuss Private deployment in a customer VPC in the EU.
[06:15] Ethan Morris: Ok thanks, please include legal and SOC docs.
[06:18] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Quick recap: action items: Diego will draft benchmark config and cost model, Maya will send pricing and contract template, we share SOC 2+KMS docs, Rivergate provides traffic profile and compliance requirements. Schedule benchmark week of 3/16, is that right?
[06:33] Tom Hargreaves: Yes, week of 3/16 works.
[06:35] Priya Kapoor: We'll get the traffic numbers to you by 3/9.
[06:38] Ethan Morris: I'll assemble the compliance checklist and share by 3/10.
[06:41] Maya Chen: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet and calendar invite for the benchmark.
[06:46] Diego Alvarez: Thanks all.
